record.paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
record.original_question: For which fields is the uniform matroid U_{a,b} representable?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3. Over which fields is Ua,b representable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a$ and $b$ be integers with $0 \le a \le b$. The uniform matroid $U_{a,b}$ is the matroid on a ground set of $b$ elements whose independent sets are exactly the subsets of size at most $a$ (equivalently, every $a$-element subset is a basis). For a field $F$, the matroid $U_{a,b}$ is said to be representable over $F$ if there exist vectors $v_1,\dots,v_b$ in some vector space over $F$ such that a subset $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,b\}$ is independent in $U_{a,b}$ if and only if $\{v_i : i\in I\}$ is linearly independent over $F$.

Determine, for each pair of integers $0 \le a \le b$, the set of fields $F$ over which the uniform matroid $U_{a,b}$ is representable.
artifact.status_search_result: The complete characterization of fields over which a uniform matroid $U_{a,b}$ is representable is widely regarded as open. It is well known that $U_{a,b}$ is representable over every sufficiently large field, and the question is closely tied to the MDS Conjecture for finite fields, which itself remains open in general (only special cases, such as for prime fields by Ball, are resolved). Recent surveys and works on matroid representability still list the precise determination of representing fields for all $U_{a,b}$ as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Matroid representation - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Uniform matroids are F-linear for all but finitely many fields F; the precise determination over finite fields is connected to the MDS conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The exact field representability of uniform matroids is unresolved in general and is linked to the open MDS conjecture.
